questions.q: A dermatologist examining a trichoscopy image identifies hair shafts that resemble a medieval weapon with a bulbous proximal end and multiple projections. This finding, known as 'Mace hair', is most characteristically associated with which condition?
questions.exp: Mace hair (resembling a medieval mace weapon) is a characteristic trichoscopic finding in loose anagen syndrome. These hairs have a ruffled cuticle and distorted proximal end due to premature keratinization of the inner root sheath.

questions.q: Identify the surgical instrument shown in the image:
questions.exp: Stainless steel holder which can fit in standard razor blades. The blade is fixed by thumbscrew

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman undergoes Minor's starch-iodine test for axillary hyperhidrosis before botulinum toxin treatment. After applying iodine solution and dusting starch powder, which color change indicates the active sweat gland areas requiring injection?
opts: Dark purple, blue, or black complex
questions.exp: In Minor's starch-iodine test, when sweat is produced, moisture facilitates a chemical reaction between iodine and starch, forming a dark purple, blue, or black complex that highlights active sweat glands. This mapped area guides precise injection placement.

questions.q: A dermatologist is comparing Tixel with fractional CO2 laser for perioral rejuvenation. Which characteristic differentiates Tixel from CO2 laser resurfacing?
opts: Uses optical energy to vaporize tissue
Creates wider craters with more charring
Relies on direct physical transfer of heat via heated metallic pins
Requires active cooling systems during the procedure
questions.exp: Tixel uses thermo-mechanical ablation through 81 pyramid-shaped pins heated to 400°C that directly transfer thermal energy to tissue upon brief contact. Unlike CO2 lasers that use optical energy, Tixel creates narrower craters with less charring and requires no anesthesia or active cooling.

questions.q: Identify the eminent figure shown:
questions.exp: Described the donor dominance principle (1959) — transplanted follicles retain DHT-resistance regardless of recipient site. Father of modern hair transplantation; also pioneered subcision for scars

questions.q: Identify the surgical instrument shown in the image:
questions.exp: Short blades with thin pointed ends. May be curved or straight

questions.q: A 58-year-old man presents with a 1.2 cm pigmented lesion on his back that is clinically suspicious for melanoma. Which biopsy technique is most appropriate for this lesion?
opts: Deep shave biopsy with saucerization technique
4 mm punch biopsy from the darkest area
Incisional biopsy of the most raised portion
questions.exp: Excisional biopsy is the preferred method for suspected melanoma as it allows complete assessment of Breslow depth and provides simultaneous diagnosis and definitive treatment with complete margin assessment. Shave biopsy is contraindicated as it compromises Breslow depth measurement, and punch biopsy carries high sampling error risk.

questions.q: During closure of an elliptical excision, the surgeon notices that one wound edge is slightly longer than the other. Which technique allows correction of this discrepancy without additional incisions?
questions.exp: The rule of halves (halving method) involves placing sutures at the midpoint of both wound edges and progressively halving the remaining segments. This technique evenly distributes the excess tissue from the longer edge without requiring additional incisions.

questions.q: A 35-year-old pianist with severe palmar hyperhidrosis is considering botulinum toxin treatment. What is the most significant complication he should be counseled about before proceeding?
opts: Permanent anhidrosis of the treated area
Transient intrinsic hand muscle weakness affecting grip
questions.exp: The most significant side effect of palmar botulinum toxin injection is transient intrinsic hand muscle weakness affecting thenar, hypothenar muscles, interossei, and pinch grip due to toxin diffusion to underlying motor nerves. This typically lasts 2-8 weeks and is particularly concerning for patients requiring fine motor dexterity.

questions.q: Which pioneer is credited with developing the first working laser, using ruby as the lasing medium in 1960?
questions.exp: Theodore Maiman constructed the first working laser in 1960 using a synthetic ruby crystal. C. Kumar N. Patel developed the CO2 laser, while Shimon Eckhouse is credited with developing IPL (Intense Pulsed Light) technology.

questions.q: A 72-year-old woman presents with a 3 cm erythematous, well-defined scaly plaque on her lower leg, confirmed as Bowen's disease on biopsy. She has peripheral vascular disease and poor wound healing. What is the expected complete response rate with MAL-PDT using a two-session protocol for this indication?
questions.exp: MAL-PDT is an approved treatment for Bowen's disease with a complete response rate of 86-93% after two sessions spaced one week apart. It is especially favored for large lesions on poor-healing sites like the lower legs of elderly patients due to superior cosmesis compared to surgery.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man undergoes photodynamic therapy for nodular basal cell carcinoma on his nose. Which pre-treatment step is strictly required to improve therapeutic efficacy in this tumor type?
opts: Application of topical retinoids for 2 weeks
questions.exp: Prior curettage (debulking) is strictly required for nodular BCC before PDT because the photosensitizer and light cannot penetrate deeply enough into thick tumors. This step improves depth penetration and therapeutic response.

questions.q: A 72-year-old diabetic patient with a heavily exuding venous leg ulcer requires a dressing change. The wound care team selects a dressing derived from brown seaweed that converts to a gel upon contact with wound exudate. What is the primary mechanism by which this dressing achieves its gel-forming property?
opts: Hydrolysis of polyurethane polymers by wound proteases
Ion-exchange reaction where calcium is exchanged for sodium
Absorption of water into hydrocolloid particles
Cross-linking of silicone molecules with wound proteins
questions.exp: Alginate dressings are derived from brown seaweed and undergo an ion-exchange reaction when calcium alginate fibers contact sodium-rich wound exudate. This calcium-sodium exchange converts the dry fibrous dressing into a soft hydrophilic gel that conforms to the wound bed.

questions.q: Identify the clinical sign / pathological finding shown:
questions.exp: Segmental narrowing of the hair shaft (a Beau's-line equivalent for hair). Reflects a transient matrix insult — chemotherapy, severe illness, or stress

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with a tense bullous eruption on her trunk. A biopsy is planned for direct immunofluorescence (DIF) studies. Which of the following is the most appropriate site and handling for the DIF specimen?
opts: Center of an intact blister, placed in 10% formalin
Perilesional skin, placed in Michel's medium
Edge of an old ruptured blister, placed in normal saline
Center of a crusted lesion, placed in Zeus medium
questions.exp: For DIF studies in bullous diseases, a biopsy of perilesional (uninvolved) skin must be obtained and placed in Michel's medium, Zeus medium, or normal saline—never formalin, which destroys immunoglobulins. The center of blisters and old lesions show secondary changes that compromise diagnosis.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman undergoes a punch biopsy for a suspicious pigmented lesion. According to Spaulding classification, what is the minimum reprocessing level required for the biopsy punch instrument?
questions.exp: Biopsy punches are classified as critical devices because they enter normally sterile tissue. Critical items require sterilization, which destroys all microbial life including bacterial spores.

questions.q: According to the Grotthuss-Draper Law, which laser-tissue interaction is essential for achieving a therapeutic photobiological effect?
questions.exp: The Grotthuss-Draper Law states that light must be absorbed by a specific target in the tissue to exert a photobiological or photothermal effect. The absorbed photon transfers its energy to the target, converting it into heat.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman undergoes excision of a benign nevus on her cheek. At the end of closure, tissue puckering is noted at one apex of the wound. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this standing cone deformity?
opts: Closure performed on a concave surface
questions.exp: Dog-ear or standing cone deformity primarily occurs when the apical angle of an elliptical excision exceeds 30 degrees, resulting from an inadequate (short/fat) ellipse design. Other causes include unequal wound edge lengths and closure over highly convex surfaces.

questions.q: A 58-year-old diabetic patient presents with a chronic non-healing ulcer on the leg. Wound culture shows bacterial growth of 10^6 CFU/g of tissue. Which of the following best explains the mechanism by which this bacterial load impairs wound healing?
opts: Direct inhibition of keratinocyte DNA synthesis
Competition for oxygen and nutrients with excessive protease release degrading ECM and growth factors
Stimulation of excessive collagen deposition leading to fibrosis
Inhibition of platelet aggregation preventing initial hemostasis
questions.exp: Bacteria above the critical threshold of 10^5 CFU/g compete with host cells for oxygen and nutrients, and stimulate an excessive inflammatory response releasing proteases like MMPs and elastase that degrade extracellular matrix components and growth factors essential for healing.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman desires laser hair removal for her legs. The dermatologist selects a wavelength of 810 nm with a pulse duration of 30 milliseconds. Which principle best explains why this pulse duration is appropriate for targeting the hair follicle?
opts: The pulse duration exceeds the thermal relaxation time of melanosomes
The pulse duration is shorter than the thermal relaxation time of the hair follicle
The pulse duration matches the thermal relaxation time of dermal collagen
The pulse duration is within the optical window spectrum
questions.exp: Terminal hair follicles (200-300 μm) have a TRT of 40-100 milliseconds. A 30 ms pulse duration is shorter than the TRT, allowing heat confinement within the follicle according to the theory of selective photothermolysis.

questions.exp: Green bottle fly — larvae used for maggot debridement therapy (MDT). Sterile larvae selectively digest necrotic tissue; ~1000 maggots applied for 1-3 days

questions.q: Identify the surgical instrument shown in the image:
questions.exp: Small size needle holder with spring action. Very thin tips for fine work

questions.q: A dermatology clinic needs to sterilize heat-sensitive plastic instruments. Which sterilization method is most appropriate, given that it produces no toxic residue and breaks down into water and oxygen?
questions.exp: Hydrogen peroxide gas plasma operates at low/room temperature making it suitable for heat-sensitive equipment, and it safely decomposes into water and oxygen without toxic residue. Ethylene oxide, while also suitable for heat-sensitive items, is highly toxic and carcinogenic requiring prolonged aeration.

questions.q: Identify the clinical sign / pathological finding shown:
questions.exp: Eosinophilic intranuclear pseudoinclusions in atypical plasma cells. Not true nuclear inclusions — invaginations of immunoglobulin-rich cytoplasm into the nucleus

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman with primary axillary hyperhidrosis undergoes MiraDry treatment. The selectivity of this device for sweat glands is primarily based on which physical principle?
opts: High electrical impedance of sweat glands compared to fat
Greater optical absorption of melanin in glandular tissue
High dipole moment of water molecules concentrated in sweat glands at the dermal-fat interface
Selective thermal conductivity of apocrine gland proteins
questions.exp: MiraDry uses microwave energy that causes dielectric heating by rotating dipole molecules. Sweat glands are water-dense structures at the dermal-fat interface, and water has a high dipole moment unlike fat, allowing selective energy absorption and thermolysis of the glands while sparing surrounding tissue.

questions.q: A patient with history of chronic alcoholism develops poor wound healing following a surgical procedure. Examination reveals perifollicular hemorrhages and corkscrew hairs. Deficiency of which nutrient is most likely responsible for impaired wound healing in this patient?
questions.exp: Vitamin C deficiency (scurvy) presents with perifollicular hemorrhages and corkscrew hairs. Vitamin C is an essential cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylase enzymes required for collagen cross-linking, and its deficiency leads to unstable collagen, poor wound strength, and wound dehiscence.

questions.q: Identify the surgical instrument shown in the image:
questions.exp: Forceps with long handles with complete ring at one end and partial at other. To pick up sterilized articles/gauze pieces from tray

questions.q: Identify the eminent figure shown:
questions.exp: Indian-American physicist who invented the CO2 laser (1964). The CO2 laser is a workhorse for ablative resurfacing and cutaneous surgery

questions.q: A 68-year-old woman with fragile skin and a Stage III sacral pressure ulcer requires frequent dressing changes. Which dressing technology would be most appropriate to minimize trauma to the periwound skin during removal?
opts: Silicone-bordered foam dressings with Safetac technology
Hydrocolloid dressings with acrylic adhesive border
questions.exp: Silicone-bordered foams (e.g., Mepilex Border) utilize soft silicone adhesive that adheres gently to intact periwound skin but not to the moist wound bed, allowing atraumatic removal without stripping fragile epithelium. This is critical for elderly patients with delicate skin.

questions.q: Identify the surgical instrument shown in the image:
questions.exp: The lower blade is blunted and the upper blade is sharp. To cut the dressing without injuring the skin
